newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine peso weakened by Thai float.
newsitem.headline: Philippine peso weakened by Thai float.

text.p: The Philippine peso was weakened early on Wednesday by a Thai government announcement it would allow a managed float of the baht, traders said.
The Philippine Central Bank had to intervene quickly in the market by selling dollars heavily at the rates of 26.377 pesos and later at 26.379 pesos.
It also offered one-day reverse repos at 20 percent from a previous 15 percent to defend the peso against speculators, traders said.
"Non-delivery forwards immediately closed their positions after the Thai announcement and bought back dollars, creating pandemonium in the market," a dealer said.
Another dealer said equity as well as interest arbitrage moneys were getting out after the Thai news.
The peso opened at 26.377 and fell to a low of 26.38 pesos to the dollar. Volume was at a hefty $471.2 million after more than an hour.
The first dealer said the peso had started to gain some strength after the Central Bank announced a 20 pct rate on a one-day reverse repo.
